title: Token Metric Narrative and Tier Guidance
content:
Executive summary:

This note lays out a concise, customer-facing narrative for why Redwood prices primarily by tokens, how to frame the unit economics in customer conversations, a recommended tier structure with rationale, and practical discounting / commitment rules for sales. It also includes short competitive context and ready-to-use talk tracks for sales and success teams. The aim is to present token pricing as the cleanest, most predictable way for customers to reason about cost per feature while giving Redwood levers (batching, KV cache, quantization) to deliver lower unit economics.

Core thesis — why token pricing (one-liner):
Tokens map directly to compute work and output volume; they let customers translate model usage into predictable cost, compare model choices, and optimize runtime settings — unlike per-request or per-inference fees which hide variability and penalize high-throughput, low-latency use cases.

Key messages to surface early:
- Token is the natural unit for LLMs: aligns with model architecture and developer mental models (prompt + completion = tokens consumed).
- Predictability and comparability: per-1K token pricing makes A/Bing model or prompt changes tractable to customers and easier to ROI.
- Operational levers: explain in plain terms how batching, prefix caching, and quantization reduce tokens’ effective cost (i.e., same token price, lower tokens-per-response).
- Flexibility: tokens cover generation + embedding + reranking under consistent units; additional per-call surcharges are confusing for engineers.

Customer personas & tailored narratives:
1) Product-first startup (PLG) — cares about predictability and ramp control
- Pain: bursty growth, unknown per-request complexity, fear of runaway bills.
- Narrative: "Start with predictable Starter credits, instrument usage per-route in the Console, and use our Optimize suggestions (batching, cache) to reduce tokens per end-user action."
- Hook: show a sample conversion: chat session average 400 tokens => cost delta when switching model or enabling KV cache.

2) Platform/Infra team (internal infra for many apps) — cares about unit economics and quotas
- Pain: chargeback across teams, need per-feature cost attribution.
- Narrative: "Chargeback per-1K tokens and use route-level SLOs. Dedicated commitments yield lower per-token pricing and predictable throughput guarantees."

3) Regulated/Enterprise customer — cares about SLAs and committed spend
- Pain: procurement wants predictable budget and contractual protections.
- Narrative: "Commit to reserved capacity or an annual token pool to qualify for enterprise discounts; you retain access controls and private deployment options if required."

Metric framing guidance (how to talk numbers) — simple rules:
- Always present price normalized to per 1,000 tokens (e.g., $X per 1K tokens) as the primary metric.
- Provide a short mapping: 1 token ≈ 4 characters ≈ 0.75 words (approx.) so customers can convert examples easily.
- Show example actions in tokens: single short assistant reply ≈ 60–150 tokens; medium search/summary ≈ 300–800 tokens; long chat session per-turn can be 1k+.
- When discussing embeddings, call out a separate per-embedding token-equivalent: e.g., embeddings billed per 1K input tokens or per vector operation (make explicit).
- Always pair price with a sample workload (table in conversation). Never lead with abstract cents/token.

Example quick-chart to use in decks (text form):
- Starter (pay-as-you-go): $0.XX per 1K tokens; 30-day free credits; no SLA.
- Growth (committed monthly): $0.YY per 1K tokens; volume discount tiers at 100M, 500M tokens; discounted embeddings by 20%.
- Enterprise Reserved: custom per 1K token; committed capacity with latency SLA and private deployment options.

Tier design rationale and guardrails:
- Keep first tier simple and transparent (low commitment, slightly higher unit price) to reduce friction for PLG adoption.
- Growth tier should incentivize predictable usage — introduce commit-based discounts and smaller volume breakpoints so mid-market customers see immediate benefit.
- Enterprise reserved pricing bundles throughput guarantees and support; large discounts are tied to upfront commit and multi-year contracts.
- Do not over-index on flat monthly plans for general-purpose inference — tokens maintain fairness across light and heavy users.

Discounting and promotional rules (sales-friendly):
- Experiment credits: marketing-led 30–90 day credits for trial cohorts, tied to onboarding playbooks.
- Volume discounts: automatic as customers cross token thresholds in a billing period; thresholds should be conservative initially (100M, 500M, 2B).
- Commit discounts: deeper discounts for committed monthly/annual pools with minimums. Commit contract must define true-ups and rollover rules.
- Time-bound promos: limited-time discounts for new products/regions; must be approved by pricing ops.
- No hidden tiers: discounts should be presented as % off per-1K token price, not complex blended rates.

Sales enablement snippets (two-liners):
- For PLG engineers: "We price per 1K tokens so you can predict cost per chat session and iterate on prompts without surprises. Use route-level quotas to cap spend during experiments."
- For procurement: "Reserved capacity gives you fixed monthly billing and service-level guarantees — we’ll model your expected token burn to recommend the right commit size."

Objection handling (common ones):
- "Tokens are confusing": show the conversions and three concrete examples for their app in 60 seconds.
- "What about embeddings/operational calls?": clarify embeddings are priced per-call or per-token-equivalent; show a worked example for your use case.
- "Requests vary in size": emphasize the benefit: tokens reflect actual compute and output; give them guardrails like quotas and usage alerts.

Competitive context (notes to internal team):
- Competitor A uses per-endpoint/seat + per-request surcharges — easier invoice line items but hides model variability and penalizes high-throughput.
- Competitor B bills per 1K tokens but with many add-on surcharges (context windows, caching tiers) which creates complexity — opportunity for Redwood to be the transparent option.
- Cloud providers sometimes push instance-hour + model license; this is attractive for extremely high throughput but requires ops sophistication; Redwood’s Dedicated + Reserved model competes here with simpler unit pricing and managed runtime.

Pricing experiments and measurement:
- A/B test two growth-tier descriptions: (A) explicit per-1K price + example use case vs (B) per-seat + included tokens to measure sign-up conversion and trial-to-paid velocity.
- Track metrics: average tokens per active user, cost per 1K tokens sold, churn by token-usage band, elasticity of demand at price changes.
- Report cadence: weekly usage trends, monthly cohort economics, quarterly model/region pricing deltas.

Operational notes for product/engineers (synced with pricing ops):
- Expose per-route token estimates in the Console and SDK (developer-visible).
- Surface Optimize suggestions near cost spikes (e.g., enable KV cache or switch to quantized variant).
- Billing must emit detailed token breakdowns by model, route, and customer tag for internal reporting and customer invoices.

Customer-facing FAQ snippets (copy suggestions):
Q: Why do you charge per token?
A: Tokens are how the models measure work — charging per 1K tokens gives a direct, comparable, and actionable way to estimate and optimize cost.

Q: How can I limit my spending?
A: Set routing quotas, per-route rate limits, and alerts in the Console. For predictable spend, choose a committed pool or Dedicated capacity.

Q: Can I negotiate discounts?
A: Yes — discounts are available for committed volumes and enterprise contracts. Our sales team models your burn and recommends the right commit size.

Action items / next steps (recommended):
- Validate the example token conversions with Applied ML to tighten the "tokens ≈ words" guidance. (owner: eng-applied-ml)
- Create a short slide pack with 3 real-customer examples (PLG, infra, enterprise) and per-action token math for sales. (owner: GTM content)
- Implement an SDK snippet that shows per-call token estimate for the three most common calls and include in the developer quickstart. (owner: developer-experience)

- Naming convention for tiers (Starter / Growth / Reserved vs other branding) — marketing input requested.
